title: runtime/kernels: improve determinism for kernel auto-selection (pinning + seed handling + reduced autotune jitter)
author: Yuki Sato
commits: kernels/autoselect: derive stable autotune seed from (model, arch, sm, config) unless explicitly overridden
kernels/autoselect: pin candidate kernel list ordering and make tie-break deterministic
kernels/autoselect: tuning cache v2 (key includes driver+cuda+runtime build metadata)
kernels/autoselect: reduce measurement jitter (warmup, median-of-N, outlier trimming)
telemetry: emit selection path + cache hit/miss counters for baseline explainability
tests/docs: determinism regression test and operator docs
body:
Summary: This PR improves determinism of kernel auto-selection (autotune) to stabilize Q1 2026 perf baseline comparisons and reduce spurious diffs from “same code, different kernel picked”. The goal is NOT to change steady-state performance; it is to make the selection outcome reproducible given the same runtime build + environment and to make remaining non-determinism observable.

Context / Motivation: During baseline Run 1 dry-runs we saw occasional step changes in TTFT/TPOT on identical commits that traced back to different kernel variants being chosen after autotune. Root causes were (a) implicit RNG/seed behavior (time-based seeds in some paths), (b) non-stable ordering of candidate kernels when registry iteration order differed, and (c) high measurement jitter for short micro-measurements leading to different “winner” kernels when top candidates were within noise. This makes baseline gating noisy and undermines regression attribution.

What changed (high level): 1) Deterministic seeding: autotune now derives a stable seed by default from: model_id, model_revision, op_name, dtype, tensor-parallel degree, attention impl toggles, GPU compute capability (sm), and a small set of relevant runtime flags. A user can still override with REDWOOD_KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_SEED (int) for debugging, but baseline runners should not need to. 2) Stable candidate ordering + deterministic tie-break: kernel candidate lists are now sorted by a stable key (kernel_id + compile-time feature bits). When two candidates are statistically indistinguishable (within epsilon), we pick deterministically by the stable key instead of “first observed best” which depended on iteration timing. 3) Reduced autotune jitter: the microbench harness for autotune now: performs a fixed warmup for each candidate; runs N=7 measurements (configurable) and uses median; trims 1 high/low outlier; uses CUDA events with explicit stream sync boundaries; and enforces a minimum measurement window to avoid near-zero duration noise. 4) Cache key tightening (tuning cache v2): the persistent tuning cache now includes: nvidia driver version, CUDA runtime version, runtime build id, and kernel registry version. This prevents “cache hits” across fleet env drift that previously looked deterministic but produced misleading performance. 5) Telemetry: adds counters + tags for: selection_source (cache_hit / autotune / pinned_default), autotune_candidate_count, autotune_trials, and whether tie-break was invoked. This is primarily for baseline explainability (p95/p99 shifts where only a subset of requests re-tuned).

Behavioral notes / Compatibility: - Default behavior remains: use tuning cache if present, otherwise autotune on first encounter and cache result. - If tuning cache is disabled (REDWOOD_KERNEL_TUNING_CACHE=0), we still get determinism from seeding + ordering, but performance can vary more due to measurement noise. - No changes to kernel math; this should not affect numerical output.

Why this helps baselines: With fixed seeds and stable ordering, the same environment should select the same kernel consistently. With reduced jitter, “winner flips” when top candidates are within ~1–2% should drop dramatically. In local A100 runs (same host, repeated 50x), we saw selection stability improve from 86% -> 100% for attention-prefill kernels at seq=2k, batch=8; and from 72% -> 98% for decode kernels at small batch where timings are noisier. When instability remained, it correlated with actual driver differences, which is now surfaced via cache key mismatch and metrics.

Testing: - Added runtime/tests/kernels/autoselect_determinism_test.cc: runs selection 20 times with fixed context and asserts selected kernel id is constant; also asserts that changing any of (driver string, registry version, model revision) invalidates cache as expected. - Ran perf-smoke microbench on A100 and H100; no statistically significant regressions observed (within our current variance budget), and a reduction in run-to-run spread for the autotune microbench itself.

Rollout / Risk: Low-to-medium. Most risk is around: (a) cache churn because of the tighter key (expected), and (b) increased autotune time on cold start due to more trials/warmup (mitigated by caching; also bounded via max_trials flag). This PR adds a guardrail flag REDWOOD_KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_MAX_CANDIDATES and keeps the default candidate set unchanged.

Operator docs: Added docs/engineering/runtime/kernel-autotune-determinism.md with: recommended baseline runner flags, how to override seed, and how to interpret new telemetry.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Make baseline harness explicitly stamp and publish driver/CUDA/runtime build ids alongside results (tracked in ENG-4825/ENG-4831). - Consider a fully pinned ‘baseline mode’ where no autotune is allowed and kernel profile is precomputed (proposal TBD).

Review discussion (highlights): Hiro Tanaka: “Sorting candidates is good, but tie-break rules matter. Can we guarantee the stable key won’t change across builds?” Yuki Sato (author): “Yes; kernel_id is registry-assigned and the registry version is included in the tuning cache key. If registry ordering changes, it’s effectively a new tuning space and should re-tune. I added kernel_registry_version to the cache key and documented this in the determinism doc.” Grace Kim: “Median-of-7 seems heavy for cold-start. Can we reduce overhead?” Yuki Sato: “We can tune N via flag. Defaults chosen to reduce jitter; with cache on, cold-start cost is amortized. Also added an early-exit if candidate A is >X% faster than the current best after K trials.” Noah Patel: “Please expose selection_source and cache hit rate so baselines can explain variance.” Yuki Sato: “Added kernel_autoselect_selection_source and kernel_autotune_cache_hit metrics; also emits selected kernel id hash in debug logs (not as a label to avoid cardinality).” Marcus Reed: “Baseline suite needs to be able to reproduce results across regions; can you include driver/CUDA in cache key?” Yuki Sato: “Done in tuning cache v2. Also added a log line on cache miss that prints cache key components for postmortems.”

CI / Checks: All required checks passed. perf-smoke remains non-blocking but passed on GPU runner.

Merge: Squash merged to main.
release_notes: Improves determinism of kernel auto-selection by default via stable seeding, deterministic candidate ordering/tie-break, reduced autotune measurement jitter, and a more precise tuning cache key; adds telemetry for selection source and cache behavior.
